description: Pulp and Paper explores how trees become paper: papermaking history, forest management and sustainability, fiber sources and pulping, how paper is made and recycled, coated and modified papers, paper products at home, and visiting a mill or plant.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: History
requirements.summary: The history of papermaking and paper’s role in society and the economy.

requirements.title: The industry and forests
requirements.summary: How the industry grows and harvests trees, sustainable forest management, and reducing pollution.

requirements.title: Fibers and pulp
requirements.summary: Trees used for papermaking, extracting fibers and bleaching pulp.

requirements.title: Making paper
requirements.summary: How paper is made and recycled, and making a sheet by hand.

requirements.title: Coated paper
requirements.summary: What coated paper is, its uses, and other ways paper is modified.

requirements.title: Paper at home
requirements.summary: Pulp and paper products found in your home.

requirements.title: A visit or research
requirements.summary: One option: visiting a mill or plant, or researching how paper products are developed.
